cues.en: Name is Martin Kleppmann. You might know me from this book that I published about a year ago called Designing Data Intensive Applications.
cues.zh: 我叫Martin Kleppmann。你们可能通过我大约一年前出版的那本书认识我，书名叫《Designing Data Intensive Applications》。

cues.en: This book is not about CRDTs.
cues.zh: 这本书不是讲CRDT的。

cues.en: Instead, it's a very broad overview of the architecture of large scale data systems and the problems of distributed systems.
cues.zh: 它其实是对大规模数据系统架构和分布式系统问题的非常广泛的概述。

cues.en: What I'm going to talk about today is a different area. So
cues.zh: 我今天要讲的是另一个领域。那么

cues.en: I am a researcher at the University of Cambridge,
cues.zh: 我是剑桥大学的研究员，

cues.en: except today, actually, I am formally on strike.
cues.zh: 不过今天，实际上我正式在罢工。

cues.en: You might have
cues.zh: 你们可能

cues.en: might have gathered. I mean this seriously. There's there's a dispute going on at the moment at many UK universities
cues.zh: 可能已经猜到了。我是认真的。目前英国很多大学正在发生一场纠纷

cues.en: where the powers that be want to essentially cut back our pension schemes in a very radical and unjustified way,
cues.zh: 当局想以一种非常激进且毫无道理的方式削减我们的养老金计划，

cues.en: which amounts to a massive pay cut and really is not justified. So, as part of this, I am on strike. I'm still going to give the talk to you
cues.zh: 这相当于大幅减薪，确实毫无道理。所以，作为其中一部分，我在罢工。我仍然会给你们做这个演讲

cues.en: because we have no problems with QCon. It's our university that we have a problem with.
cues.zh: 因为我们和QCon没有问题。有问题的是我们的大学。

cues.en: But just to say that I am giving this talk as a private individual who happens to be interested in distributed systems
cues.zh: 但需要说明，我是以个人身份做这个演讲的，我只是碰巧对分布式系统感兴趣

cues.en: rather than as an employee of the University of Cambridge.
cues.zh: 而不是作为剑桥大学的雇员。

cues.en: Okay. So let's talk about some technical stuff. So what I'd like to talk about is collaborative applications.
cues.zh: 好。那我们聊点技术的东西。我想谈的是协作应用。

cues.en: And so a classic example of this would be Google Docs. So there, as you know, you can have several people who can all collaborate in a document. They can edit the document at the same time without having to email it back and forth, which is very convenient.
cues.zh: 一个经典例子就是Google Docs。如你们所知，在那里可以让多个人协作编辑一个文档。他们可以同时编辑文档，而不必来回发邮件，这非常方便。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: what we want in this kind of systems is that eventually, like, even though several people might be editing the document at the same time, they should all end up with the same document on their screen at the end. So this is what we call a convergence property. Everyone should end up, as they communicate, having the same state.
cues.zh: 在这类系统中，我们希望最终达到这样的效果：即使多人可能同时编辑同一份文档，他们最后也都能在屏幕上得到相同的文档。这就是我们所说的收敛性。随着彼此通信，每个人最终都应该拥有相同的状态。

cues.en: So if you were here this morning, Heidi Howard gave a great talk on consensus,
cues.zh: 如果你今天上午在现场，Heidi Howard 做了一场关于共识的精彩演讲，

cues.en: which is also about getting several nodes in the distributed system to agree on something.
cues.zh: 共识同样是让分布式系统中的多个节点就某件事达成一致。

cues.en: So it looks like superficially the problem that we have here is kind of similar to consensus.
cues.zh: 所以表面上看，我们这里遇到的问题似乎和共识有点类似。

cues.en: So as we'll explain later in this talk, actually this is a very different kind of problem. Even though it looks superficially similar, the properties that it has are fundamentally different, and comparing those two will be an interesting part of this talk.
cues.zh: 不过，正如我们稍后会在演讲中解释的那样，实际上这是完全不同的一类问题。虽然表面上看起来相似，但它们具备的性质有着根本区别，而比较两者会是本次演讲中很有意思的一部分。

cues.en: Okay, so let's take a scenario that is probably familiar to you. This is you, a little blue stick figure, who is hacking on some code on your laptop,
cues.zh: 好，我们来看一个你可能很熟悉的场景。这个小蓝人代表你，你正在笔记本电脑上编写代码，

cues.en: and you make some changes. You edit some source files. You save them to your local disk. At some point, you decide
cues.zh: 然后你做了一些修改。你编辑了一些源文件，把它们保存到本地磁盘。某个时候，你决定

cues.en: you're ready to share this code with your colleagues, and so you commit it to your favorite version control system, and then you maybe push it to a centralized repository, maybe to GitHub or something like that, some mechanism
cues.zh: 已经准备好把代码分享给同事了，于是你将它提交到自己喜欢的版本控制系统中，然后可能再把它推送到一个中央仓库，比如 GitHub 之类的地方，通过某种机制

cues.en: by which you can send your commits to your coworkers.
cues.zh: 把你的提交发送给同事。

cues.en: And so at the same time, while you've been editing the code, maybe your colleague, who is this pink stick figure,
cues.zh: 所以与此同时，当你一直在编辑代码时，也许你的同事，也就是这个粉色的小人，

cues.en: has also been editing the code, has also been changing it, maybe also making commits,
cues.zh: 也在编辑代码、修改代码，甚至可能也在提交代码，

cues.en: and what you end up now with is that
cues.zh: 这样一来，最终就会出现这种情况：

cues.en: if this colleague wants to also push their changes to the server, they will first have to fetch
cues.zh: 如果这位同事也想把自己的修改推送到服务器，就必须先拉取（fetch）你推送的提交，

cues.en: the commit that you pushed and have to merge those together.
cues.zh: 然后将双方的修改合并起来。

cues.en: And so, as you've probably experienced before,
cues.zh: 所以，你可能之前已经遇到过这种情况：

cues.en: this kind of merge
cues.zh: 这种合并操作

cues.en: is straightforward if you were editing two different files, because in that case, Git just knows, well, two different files, I'm just going to merge them together. Those changes are independent.
cues.zh: 如果你们编辑的是两个不同的文件，那就很简单，因为 Git 知道这是两个不同的文件，直接把它们合并就行了。这些修改互不影响。

cues.en: If one of you changed the top of a file and the other one changed the bottom of the same file, then that's probably still fine as well, because the changes are far enough
cues.zh: 如果一个人修改了文件顶部，另一个人修改了同一个文件的底部，那通常也没问题，因为两处修改相隔足够远，

cues.en: apart in the file that git just says, okay, I'll merge those automatically.
cues.zh: Git 就会说，好吧，我来自动合并这些修改。

cues.en: But if you were editing actually the same lines, then you've got a merge conflict that you need to resolve manually.
cues.zh: 但如果你们修改的恰好是同几行代码，那就会产生合并冲突，需要你手动解决。

cues.en: So if we look at this kind of system more abstractly, you can say there are a couple of nodes. These might be like your laptop and your phone, or they might be servers in a data center. We don't really care too much. They're just some kind of computing nodes, each of which can store some data, and when you want to edit that data, you make a change to your local copy, which might, in the case of the source code, is the source code files living on your local hard disk.
cues.zh: 如果我们更抽象地来看这种系统，可以把它看作由几个节点组成。这些节点可能是你的笔记本电脑和手机，也可能是数据中心里的服务器。具体是什么并不重要。它们只是某种计算节点，每个节点都能存储一些数据。当你想要编辑这些数据时，就会修改本地副本。比如在源代码这个场景中，本地副本就是存储在你电脑硬盘上的源代码文件。

cues.en: You change that, and then at some point, those changes get communicated to anyone else who also has a copy of that data, so to any other nodes.
cues.zh: 你修改了数据，然后某个时刻，这些改动会被传达给其他也拥有该数据副本的人，也就是其他节点。

cues.en: And so while this is going on, maybe a purple user can simultaneously be making some change to their copy of the data, and they similarly will then forward on those changes to the other users. And so whether
cues.zh: 在这个过程中，可能一个紫色用户同时在修改他们的数据副本，同样地，他们随后也会把这些改动转发给其他用户。所以无论是

cues.en: these changes here are via git push, via this kind of explicit operation, or if you're using Google Docs, these kind of changes are sent automatically,
cues.zh: 这里的改动是通过 git push 这种显式操作，还是你用的是 Google Docs，这类改动都是自动发送的，

cues.en: continuously in the background.
cues.zh: 在后台持续进行。

cues.en: So in the case of Google Docs,
cues.zh: 所以在 Google Docs 的情况下，

cues.en: this
cues.zh: 这个

cues.en: local copy that you apply the changes to is living in memory in your web browser. So in the tab that you've opened the Google Doc in, when you type a letter and you change the document, that change gets immediately applied to your local copy of the document. So it doesn't wait for a round trip to the server before showing the letter that you just typed on your own screen, because that would take too long. So what Google Docs does in that case is it immediately applies the change locally,
cues.zh: 你应用改动的本地副本存在于你浏览器内存中。也就是你打开 Google Doc 的那个标签页里，当你输入一个字母、修改文档时，这个改动会立即应用到你的本地文档副本上。所以它不会等你和服务器往返一趟才把你刚输入的字母显示在屏幕上，因为那样太慢了。所以 Google Docs 在这种情况下做的就是立即在本地应用改动，

cues.en: and then asynchronously
cues.zh: 然后异步地

cues.en: in the background,
cues.zh: 在后台，

cues.en: which might take a few seconds or whatever, it sends on the change to the server, who then sends on the change to anyone else who's got a copy of that document open. And so you kind of get the same kind of property that several people can make changes independently without knowing about each other's changes,
cues.zh: 可能需要几秒钟之类的，把改动发送到服务器，服务器再把改动发送给其他打开了该文档副本的人。于是你就得到了类似的特性：多个人可以各自独立地修改，而不知道彼此的改动，

cues.en: just like you get with
cues.zh: 就像你用

cues.en: git commits, just on a shorter time scale. But you still have exactly the same concurrency issue.
cues.zh: git commit 时那样，只是时间尺度更短。但你仍然会遇到完全相同的并发问题。

cues.en: In particular,
cues.zh: 尤其是，

cues.en: this concurrency issue becomes more
cues.zh: 如果你有离线编辑，这个并发问题会变得

cues.en: obvious if you have offline editing.
cues.zh: 更加明显。

cues.en: So in this case, you can think of this as a network partition
cues.zh: 所以在这种情况下，你可以把它看作网络分区

cues.en: that is separating
cues.zh: 将其中一个节点

cues.en: one of the nodes from the rest of the system, and so the pink user might still be changing
cues.zh: 与系统其余部分隔离开来，所以粉色用户可能仍在修改

cues.en: their local copy of the document,
cues.zh: 他们本地的文档副本，

cues.en: but they can't send the changes to any of the other users because they are offline right now. They don't have an internet connection
cues.zh: 但他们无法将更改发送给其他任何用户，因为他们现在处于离线状态。他们没有网络连接

cues.en: or because there's some network disruption, and so in that case, the changes will stay local to their own machine, and then only sometime later, once the network is restored, those changes will then be flushed. But what we still want in that case is for those changes to be merged together.
cues.zh: 或者因为存在某些网络中断，所以在这种情况下，更改会保留在他们自己的机器上，然后只有过了一段时间，网络恢复后，这些更改才会被刷新出去。但在那种情况下，我们仍然希望这些更改能够被合并在一起。

cues.en: So taking this
cues.zh: 所以拿这个

cues.en: of Google Docs again as an example,
cues.zh: 再以 Google Docs 为例，

cues.en: you can let's take the state of the thing that we're working on as a text document. So this is like just a sequence of characters
cues.zh: 你可以把我们正在处理的东西的状态看作一个文本文档。所以这就像是一串字符

cues.en: which currently read hello.
cues.zh: 目前读作 hello。

cues.en: So you have two users who concurrently update this document. The pink user adds the
cues.zh: 所以有两个用户同时更新这个文档。粉色用户在感叹号前

cues.en: word world before the exclamation mark,
cues.zh: 添加了 world 这个词，

cues.en: and the blue user adds a smiley face after the exclamation mark.
cues.zh: 而蓝色用户在感叹号后添加了一个笑脸。

cues.en: And so now, if this was git, this would probably be a merge conflict that you would have to resolve manually,
cues.zh: 那么现在，如果这是 git，这可能会是一个合并冲突，你必须手动解决，

cues.en: but if you've tried this kind of thing in Google Docs, it turns out that actually Google Docs never prompts you to
cues.zh: 但如果你在 Google Docs 里试过这类操作，结果发现 Google Docs 实际上从不会提示你

cues.en: resolve a merge conflict.
cues.zh: 去解决合并冲突。

cues.en: It will always just merge the changes automatically
cues.zh: 它会自动合并更改

cues.en: based on what it thinks is a sensible way of merging this, and in this case, we can actually define quite a sensible way of merging it because we can say, well, the world clearly came before the exclamation mark, the smiley face came after the exclamation mark, so we can just preserve both of those insertions,
cues.zh: 基于它认为合理的合并方式，在这个例子中，我们其实可以定义一种相当合理的合并方式，因为我们可以说，很明显 world 在感叹号之前，笑脸在感叹号之后，所以我们只要保留这两个插入内容，

cues.en: and so a sensible
cues.zh: 所以一个合理的

cues.en: final merged state is hello world exclamation mark smiley,
cues.zh: 最终合并状态就是 hello world 感叹号笑脸，

cues.en: and this is in fact what Google Docs will do. But we're not limited to only text documents, so let's look at a different data type. You could use a set, for example. So a set is just some unordered collection of elements,
cues.zh: 这实际上就是 Google Docs 的做法。但我们不局限于文本文档，来看看另一种数据类型。比如可以用集合。集合就是一些无序元素的集合，

cues.en: and you could have the red user maybe removes the item B from the set. It was previously AB removes B, so only A is left.
cues.zh: 红色用户可能从集合中移除了元素 B。之前是 AB，移除 B 后只剩下 A。

cues.en: Concurrently, while that is happening,
cues.zh: 与此同时，

cues.en: the purple user decides to add a new element, C, to the set, written here with that set union operator,
cues.zh: 紫色用户决定向集合中添加新元素 C，这里用集合并运算符表示，

cues.en: so the set then is merged ABC.
cues.zh: 于是集合合并后是 ABC。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: as those two changes get propagated from one node to the other, again, we can just define what we consider to be a sensible merged outcome,
cues.zh: 当这两个更改从一个节点传播到另一个节点时，同样，我们只需定义我们认为合理的合并结果，

cues.en: and in this case I'm going to say, well, A was not touched by either user, so we're just going to leave A there. B was removed by one of the users. C was added by one of the users, so we want in the final state to contain c but not b, and so we just say a and c is a sensible merged outcome in this case.
cues.zh: 在这个例子中我会说，A 没有被任何用户改动，所以我们就保留 A。B 被其中一个用户移除了。C 被其中一个用户添加了，所以最终状态应包含 C 但不包含 B，因此我们说 A 和 C 在这种情况下是合理的合并结果。

cues.en: One more example.
cues.zh: 再举一个例子。

cues.en: I consider a counter. So maybe like the number of likes on a Facebook post or something like that would be a counter that you can increment,
cues.zh: 我想用计数器来举例。比如 Facebook 帖子上的点赞数之类的，就是一个可以递增的计数器，

cues.en: and so here, let's say we're starting in the initial state where the counter value is one,
cues.zh: 这里假设初始状态下计数器的值是 1，

cues.en: and you have two users who both increment that counter. So they both change the value from one to two.
cues.zh: 然后有两个用户都对这个计数器做了递增。他们都把值从 1 改成了 2。

cues.en: Now you could say that, well, both users are in the same state, so
cues.zh: 你可能会说，这两个用户处于相同的状态，所以

cues.en: we should just consider two to be the merged final state.
cues.zh: 我们直接把 2 当作合并后的最终状态就行了。

cues.en: But that would actually lose information,
cues.zh: 但这样其实会丢失信息，

cues.en: because here we know from inspecting the set of changes that happened
cues.zh: 因为从实际发生的变更集合来看，

cues.en: that actually two increment operations happened. So really what we want is for both increment operations to still take effect in the final result. So what we want is that the final result is actually three, because we started with one, and then one user incremented it, the other user incremented it. The order in which you do those two increments doesn't matter, but the final value should be three. So what this is saying is that we need to consider not just the state, the value at any one time, because if we just compare two and two, they look the same, but actually we need to capture the sequence of changes that were made to the data and reapply those, and that will allow us to reach a sensible merged outcome.
cues.zh: 实际上发生了两次递增操作。所以我们真正想要的是，两次递增操作在最终结果中都生效。也就是说，最终结果应该是 3，因为初始值是 1，然后一个用户递增了它，另一个用户也递增了它。这两次递增的先后顺序无所谓，但最终值应该是 3。这就是说，我们不能只看状态，只看某一时刻的值，因为如果只比较 2 和 2，它们看起来一样，但实际上我们需要记录对数据所做的变更序列，并重新应用这些变更，这样才能得到合理的合并结果。

cues.en: Okay, so this problem of people editing stuff simultaneously and having to merge it has been studied for a rather long time, and there are, at a high level, two families of algorithms that were developed. One is operational transformation, which has been studied by academics since the late 80s,
cues.zh: 好，这个多人同时编辑并需要合并的问题，已经被研究很久了。从高层来看，主要有两大类算法。一类是操作转换，学术界从 80 年代末就开始研究，

cues.en: and which is actually the foundation of Google Docs. So Google Docs internally uses an operational transformation algorithm.
cues.zh: 它实际上就是 Google Docs 的基础。Google Docs 内部用的就是操作转换算法。

cues.en: However, due to some problems that I'll explain in a minute, people got rather frustrated with operational transformation in the early 2000s
cues.zh: 不过，因为一些问题——我稍后会解释——人们在 2000 年代初对操作转换相当失望，

cues.en: and then started this separate direction of research
cues.zh: 于是开始了另一个研究方向，

cues.en: called conflict free replicated data types, or CRDTs for short.
cues.zh: 叫做无冲突复制数据类型，简称 CRDT。

cues.en: CRDTs has been the focus of our research. So let me just give you a bit of historical background because it's kind of interesting,
cues.zh: CRDT 一直是我们研究的重点。我先给大家一点历史背景，因为这挺有意思的，

cues.en: and also some motivation for why we wanted CRDTs.
cues.zh: 也说说我们为什么想要 CRDT。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: as I mentioned, a whole bunch of people across research community
cues.zh: 正如我提到的，研究界的一大群人

cues.en: have proposed
cues.zh: 提出了

cues.en: operational transformation algorithms.
cues.zh: 操作转换算法。

cues.en: So the first one's in the late '80s, and the paper reads quite nicely, it kind of makes sense and looks plausible when you read it, except you
cues.zh: 最早的一篇在 80 年代末，论文读起来挺不错，讲得通，乍看也合理，只是你

cues.en: didn't then realize, reading some more papers, that actually, a few years after this was published, people discovered that this application was that this algorithm was simply wrong. So what I mean with wrong is what these algorithms are supposed to achieve is convergence. That is, everybody ends up with the same document on their screen at the end if no more edits are happening. However, this algorithm did not achieve convergence.
cues.zh: 当时没意识到——多读些论文后才发现——其实这篇发表几年后，人们发现这个算法根本就是错的。我说的错，是指这些算法本应实现收敛。也就是说，如果不再有编辑，最后每个人屏幕上都是同一份文档。但这个算法没有实现收敛。

cues.en: There were certain edge cases
cues.zh: 有一些特定的边缘情况

cues.en: where certain edits could happen concurrently where you would end up permanently diverged,
cues.zh: 某些编辑可能并发发生，最终导致永久分叉，

cues.en: so these two different copies would be permanently out of sync with each other and never become consistent again.
cues.zh: 于是这两个不同副本会永久不同步，再也无法恢复一致。

cues.en: So that is kind of a problem. So of course, people thought about this a bit harder and proposed another algorithm.
cues.zh: 所以这算是个问题。于是人们当然更深入地思考了这件事，提出了另一种算法。

cues.en: Unfortunately, a few years later, that one also turned out to be wrong. It had a very similar bug, and this story just kept continuing.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，几年后，那个算法也被证明是错的。它有一个非常类似的缺陷，而这样的故事还在继续。

cues.en: So over the course of about two decades,
cues.zh: 所以在约二十年的时间里，

cues.en: all of these algorithms were proposed and then only a few years later to discover that it's wrong. So a real bloodbath of failed algorithms here.
cues.zh: 所有这些算法被提出，然后仅仅几年后就被发现是错的。这里真是一场失败算法的血雨腥风。

cues.en: We did end up with a couple of algorithms which are correct, and in fact Google Docs is based on one of those that is not wrong,
cues.zh: 我们最终确实得到了几个正确的算法，事实上 Google Docs 就是基于其中一个不出错的算法，

cues.en: but the particular property of those remaining ones is that they require a centralized server.
cues.zh: 但这些保留下来的算法有一个特殊性质：它们需要一台中心化服务器。

cues.en: So they restrict
cues.zh: 所以它们限制了

cues.en: the communication flows in the system so that if the pink user here changes something and the purple user has changed something,
cues.zh: 系统中的通信流向，使得如果这里的粉色用户改了某些东西，而紫色用户也改了某些东西，

cues.en: the changes they make have to be exchanged via this central server. So it's not allowed for them to have some kind of back channel or some kind of other communication paths on the side, because if they had that, they would break the assumptions
cues.zh: 他们所做出的更改必须通过这台中心服务器来交换。不允许他们拥有某种旁路通道或某种其他侧路通信路径，因为如果有的话，就会破坏

cues.en: of the algorithm, and it would no longer achieve this convergence.
cues.zh: 算法的假设，它就不再能实现这种收敛了。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: this is a severe restriction here. All of the communication has to go via Google server,
cues.zh: 这是一个很大的限制。所有通信都必须经过 Google 服务器，

cues.en: even if it's just like syncing some data between your phone and your laptop, and they are like 50 centimeters away from each other. You still have to go via a data center in Virginia or whatever, which is kind of ridiculous if you think about it. So what I'm interested in is generalizing this model so that actually you can just have any communication topology in the system. So for example, if the blue user here has two devices, a phone and a laptop, and they want to synchronize some data, and the pink user also has two devices, well, they should just be able to synchronize via local network or whatever
cues.zh: 哪怕只是在手机和笔记本电脑之间同步点数据，而它们彼此距离也就 50 厘米左右。你依然得绕道弗吉尼亚州之类的数据中心，仔细想想这挺荒谬的。所以我感兴趣的是将这种模型泛化，让系统可以支持任意通信拓扑。比如，这里的蓝色用户有手机和笔记本两台设备，想要同步一些数据，而粉色用户也有两台设备，那他们理应可以直接通过局域网或者任何

cues.en: connectivity they happen to have, even if they're actually not connected to the Internet right now. So
cues.zh: 手头现有的连接方式进行同步，即便他们此时根本没有连上互联网。所以

cues.en: this
cues.zh: 这种

cues.en: kind of communication pattern simply won't work in the Google Docs case because you cannot safely have this communication directly between devices without going through the central server.
cues.zh: 通信模式在 Google Docs 中根本行不通，因为不经过中央服务器，设备之间就无法安全地直接通信。

cues.en: So I think it would be really great if applications
cues.zh: 所以我认为，如果应用程序

cues.en: can not depend on this central server, be more decentralized,
cues.zh: 能够不依赖中央服务器，变得更加去中心化，那就太棒了，

cues.en: so that you can actually just use whatever network is available,
cues.zh: 这样你就可以直接利用手头任何可用的网络，

cues.en: and then at some point later, if connectivity is reestablished,
cues.zh: 然后在随后的某个时刻，如果连接恢复了，

cues.en: then of course the nodes should be able to synchronize again using the Internet.
cues.zh: 节点自然就能再次通过互联网进行同步。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: this is a more kind of decentralized pattern for building applications,
cues.zh: 这是一种更去中心化的应用构建模式，

cues.en: and when I talk about decentralization,
cues.zh: 当我谈到去中心化时，

cues.en: people inevitably ask, Is that something to do with blockchains?
cues.zh: 人们总会问，这和区块链有关吗？

cues.en: Because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: a lot of people in the blockchain community
cues.zh: 区块链社区里很多人

cues.en: who are interested in building these
cues.zh: 热衷于构建这些

cues.en: systems
cues.zh: 系统

cues.en: without trust in a central server
cues.zh: 不依赖中心化服务器

cues.en: also label their work under the heading of decentralization.
cues.zh: 他们也将自己的工作归在去中心化这个标题下。

cues.en: So I'm personally not all that interested in blockchains. I'm happy for other people to work on it,
cues.zh: 所以我个人对区块链并不太感兴趣。我很乐意让别人去做，

cues.en: but let me just compare the two briefly because it is such a frequently asked question.
cues.zh: 但让我简单比较一下两者，因为这是经常被问到的问题。

cues.en: So as you probably know, a blockchain consists of some blocks of data.
cues.zh: 你们可能知道，区块链由一些数据区块组成。

cues.en: Each subsequent block contains a hash of the previous block, a cryptographic hash, and that means then if you have a signature on the last block, can follow through the hashes and you're guaranteed the integrity
cues.zh: 每个后续区块都包含前一个区块的哈希，一种密码学哈希，这意味着如果你对最后一个区块有签名，就可以顺着哈希追溯，从而保证

cues.en: of this entire sequence of blocks. And then there might be some mercurly trees and stuff like that which allow you to cryptographically prove that a certain record appears in this chain, and so that's like the foundation for bitcoin transactions and such like.
cues.zh: 整个区块序列的完整性。然后可能还有默克尔树之类的东西，让你能以密码学方式证明某条记录出现在这个链中，这就是比特币交易等的基础。

cues.en: Moreover,
cues.zh: 此外，

cues.en: what you have in most of these blockchain protocols is some kind of consensus protocol
cues.zh: 大多数区块链协议中都有某种共识协议

cues.en: which decides what the next block in the chain is going to be,
cues.zh: 来决定链上的下一个区块是什么，

cues.en: and typically those are Byzantine consensus protocols, which just means that they can tolerate
cues.zh: 通常这些是拜占庭共识协议，意思就是它们能容忍

cues.en: some of the nodes actually being actively malicious
cues.zh: 部分节点实际上 actively 恶意

cues.en: and still, so despite the presence of malicious nodes,
cues.zh: 并且，尽管存在恶意节点，

cues.en: this thing will agree on the next block.
cues.zh: 这东西仍能就下一个区块达成一致。

cues.en: So this agreement property is quite strong that you get in blockchains.
cues.zh: 所以这种一致性属性在区块链中是非常强的。

cues.en: So in particular,
cues.zh: 所以具体来说，

cues.en: what the protocol is supposed to guarantee is, if there are no forks, you have this linear sequence of blocks.
cues.zh: 协议应该保证的是，如果没有分叉，你就有一条线性的区块序列。

cues.en: It's a totally ordered sequence,
cues.zh: 这是一个全序序列，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: there's this decision process which ensures that no conflicting transactions get put into the same block. So what this means is
cues.zh: 有这样一个决策过程，确保没有冲突的交易被放进同一个区块。所以这意味着

cues.en: if you're wanting to prevent a user from spending the same coin twice,
cues.zh: 如果你想防止用户把同一枚币花两次，

cues.en: you have to make a decision as to whether this transaction or that transaction that they made using the same coin is the valid one. So what you need here is consensus,
cues.zh: 你就必须做出决定：他们用同一枚币做的这笔交易还是那笔交易才是有效的。所以这里你需要的是共识，

cues.en: which if there are several conflicting proposed transactions, it picks one, and that is what prevents double spending in these cryptocurrencies.
cues.zh: 当存在多笔冲突的候选交易时，它挑出其中一笔，而这正是防止这些加密货币中双重花费的机制。

cues.en: So that is the fundamental abstraction of consensus.
cues.zh: 这就是共识的基本抽象。

cues.en: There are several proposed values potentially conflicting,
cues.zh: 有多个可能冲突的候选值，

cues.en: and what the consensus protocol does is to decide on one of them and to throw away the others.
cues.zh: 而共识协议所做的就是决定其中一个，并丢弃其余的。

cues.en: And that is exactly what you want in the case of a blockchain, and it's exactly what you don't want in the case of collaborating on the document. Because if you think about it, if you make some changes to a document and your colleague makes some changes to the document, what a consensus protocol would do is to choose to choose the changes from one of you and throw the other one away, which is actually... It would probably make you a bit unhappy.
cues.zh: 这正是你在区块链场景中想要的，也恰恰是你在协作编辑文档时不想要的。因为你想一想，如果你对文档做了一些修改，你的同事也做了一些修改，共识协议会怎么做——它会选择你们中一个人的修改，把另一个人的丢掉，这实际上……这可能会让你有点不爽。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: what we want here for collaboration protocols is to keep all of the changes that were made and to merge them in such a way that they converge towards the same state. So that is what I mean with this thing looks superficially like consensus and is really different because consensus is fundamentally around this idea of choosing one.
cues.zh: 对于协作协议，我们想要的是保留所有已做的更改，并以一种能让它们收敛到相同状态的方式合并它们。所以我说的就是这个东西表面上看起来像共识，但实际上完全不同，因为共识本质上是围绕选择某一个这个理念。

cues.en: Okay, so
cues.zh: 好的，那么

cues.en: back to those two families of algorithms for achieving convergence. Going to talk briefly about some research that we did on CRDTs.
cues.zh: 回到那两类实现收敛的算法。我要简要谈谈我们在CRDT上做的一些研究。

cues.en: So CRDTs are also a family
cues.zh: 所以CRDT也是一类

cues.en: of data structures which several people on different nodes can update concurrently
cues.zh: 数据结构，不同节点上的多个人可以并发更新

cues.en: and which will automatically merge the changes together,
cues.zh: 并且会自动将更改合并在一起，

cues.en: very much like those examples I showed earlier in this talk. And they've been used in a few practical systems, so for example, the Atom text editor just recently released a calibration feature that is built on CRDTs.
cues.zh: 非常像我之前在这个演讲中展示的那些例子。它们已经被用在一些实际系统中，比如Atom文本编辑器最近发布了一个基于CRDT的协作功能。

cues.en: The React database used them internally for merging things and so on.
cues.zh: React数据库在内部用它们来合并内容等等。

cues.en: So given this
cues.zh: 所以考虑到

cues.en: poor history of problems with operational transformation algorithms,
cues.zh: 操作转换算法糟糕的问题历史，

cues.en: what we wanted to do is to be really sure that we're not repeating the same problems with CRDTs.
cues.zh: 我们想要做的是确保我们不会在CRDT上重复同样的问题。

cues.en: So we want to prove formally,
cues.zh: 所以我们想要形式化地证明，

cues.en: mathematically,
cues.zh: 数学上，

cues.en: that these CRDTs really do converge, that they really do behave
cues.zh: 这些CRDT确实会收敛，它们确实会按

cues.en: as they're supposed to, because as we saw with the problems with the OT algorithms,
cues.zh: 预期的方式运作，因为正如我们在OT算法的问题中看到的，

cues.en: some of these algorithms can be quite subtle, and just like thinking about it informally,
cues.zh: 其中一些算法可能相当微妙，仅仅非形式化地思考，

cues.en: you might not be able to fully convince yourself that it really, under all circumstances,
cues.zh: 你可能无法完全说服自己它在所有情况下

cues.en: does converge. So what we did is we used Isabelle, which is a theorem proving software,
cues.zh: 确实会收敛。所以我们做的是使用Isabelle，这是一个定理证明软件，

cues.en: which you can use to write down formally the properties that
cues.zh: 你可以用它形式化地写下

cues.en: you want. And so we use this software to write down several CRDT algorithms. So RGA is a text editing CRDT.
cues.zh: 你想要的属性。所以我们用这个软件写下了几个CRDT算法。RGA就是一个文本编辑CRDT。

cues.en: OPSET is a set, and the counter is like what I showed earlier.
cues.zh: OPSET 是一个集合，计数器就像我之前展示的那样。

cues.en: And we can show that they
cues.zh: 而且我们可以证明它们

cues.en: satisfy
cues.zh: 满足

cues.en: a consistency property called strong eventual consistency,
cues.zh: 一种叫强最终一致性的—致性属性，

cues.en: which in particular implies convergence.
cues.zh: 这尤其意味着收敛。

cues.en: And so we can show that
cues.zh: 所以我们可以证明

cues.en: these data
cues.zh: 这些数据

cues.en: satisfy this consistency property under certain assumptions,
cues.zh: 在某些假设下满足这一致性属性，

cues.en: but now how do we know that those assumptions are valid? We now have a second layer of proof
cues.zh: 但我们现在怎么知道这些假设是有效的？我们现在有了第二层证明

cues.en: in which we have a model of a network. It's a very unreliable network. It's allowed to throw away any number of messages, reorder messages,
cues.zh: 我们有一个网络模型。这是个非常不可靠的网络。它允许丢弃任意数量的消息、重排消息，

cues.en: and what we prove here is that those assumptions,
cues.zh: 我们在这里证明的是，那些假设，

cues.en: under which this strong eventual consistency holds,
cues.zh: 在这种条件下，这种强最终一致性成立，

cues.en: are satisfied in all possible executions
cues.zh: 在所有可能的执行中都得到满足

cues.en: of this network model. So no matter how badly the network tries to mess things up, we can prove that these algorithms will always satisfy the guarantees they claim. So unfortunately, I don't have time to talk about this theoretical work in any more detail.
cues.zh:
对于这个网络模型。无论网络试图如何恶意干扰，我们都可以证明，这些算法始终能够满足它们所承诺的保证。

很遗憾，我没有时间进一步详细介绍这方面的理论研究。

cues.en: If you're interested, there's a URL there at the bottom of the paper. It's reasonably readable even if you don't have prior experience in formal verification of algorithms,
cues.zh: 如果你感兴趣，论文底部有个 URL。即使你之前没有算法形式验证的经验，这篇论文也相当易读，

cues.en: so do have a look at that.
cues.zh: 那不妨去看看。

cues.en: What I do want to spend a bit more time talking about is automerge,
cues.zh: 我想多花点时间讲讲 automerge，

cues.en: which is an application,
cues.zh: 这是一个应用，

cues.en: an implementation of these ideas that we've been working on. This is an open source library in JavaScript.
cues.zh: 这是我们在这些想法上的一个实现。这是一个用 JavaScript 编写的开源库。

cues.en: In principle, you could implement it in any language, but I guess JavaScript is very portable across many platforms, which is why we're using that at the moment.
cues.zh: 原则上，你可以用任何语言来实现它，但我猜JavaScript在很多平台上都有很好的可移植性，这就是我们现在用它的原因。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: you can think of this as a data model layer or data structure library
cues.zh: 你可以把它看作是一个数据模型层或数据结构库

cues.en: on top of which you can build collaborative applications.
cues.zh: 在此基础上，你可以构建协作应用。

cues.en: So what it gives you is an abstraction that looks very much like JSON,
cues.zh: 所以它提供给你的是一种非常像JSON的抽象，

cues.en: and you can modify this JSON document and use that to build applications on top of it. So I'll show you some examples of prototype applications
cues.zh: 你可以修改这个JSON文档，并用它来构建应用。接下来我会展示一些原型应用的例子

cues.en: that we built using this.
cues.zh: 这些是我们用它构建的。

cues.en: The first one is called Trellis. It's a clone of Trello,
cues.zh: 第一个叫做Trellis。它是Trello的克隆版，

cues.en: the popular project management tool. Looks like this. So just like Trello,
cues.zh: Trello是一个流行的项目管理工具。它看起来是这样的。就像Trello一样，

cues.en: you have columns and you have cards in those columns,
cues.zh: 你有列，列里有卡片，

cues.en: and you can drag and drop the cards between columns. This here is a superhero recruiting initiative that we've used as an example.
cues.zh: 你可以在列之间拖放卡片。这里是一个超级英雄招募计划，我们把它作为示例。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: you can assign columns to people and you can leave comments on cars and so on, all the typical stuff you would expect.
cues.zh: 你可以把列分配给人员，可以在卡片上留言等等，所有你会想到的典型功能都有。

cues.en: The cool thing with this is that it's implemented without any servers at all. So we are able to do this based on a peer to peer networking model using WebRTC,
cues.zh: 很酷的一点是，它完全不需要任何服务器就能实现。所以我们可以基于使用WebRTC的点对点网络模型来做到这一点，

cues.en: which is normally what enables video calls in your web browser, but you can use it for transferring data as well. In particular,
cues.zh: WebRTC通常是在你的网页浏览器中启用视频通话的技术，但你也可以用它来传输数据。特别是，

cues.en: we can transfer the edits made to a CRDT
cues.zh: 我们可以把对CRDT所做的编辑

cues.en: over something like WebRTC, and there's bit of user interface here on the right hand side for managing that network.
cues.zh: 通过类似WebRTC的方式传输，右侧这里有一些用户界面来管理那个网络。

cues.en: And moreover, what it does, it keeps track of all of the changes that happened.
cues.zh: 而且，它会记录所有发生的变化。

cues.en: So whenever you move a card around or you update a card or whatever, it actually appears in this log of changes here
cues.zh: 所以每当你移动卡片、更新卡片之类的操作，实际上都会出现在右下角这个变更日志里。

cues.en: on the bottom right hand side. So that's just one example app that we built on top of automerge.
cues.zh: 这只是我们在 automerge 之上构建的一个示例应用。

cues.en: Another example is an app we call Pixel Pusher, which is quite a fun one. It's a collaborative pixel art editor.
cues.zh: 另一个例子是我们叫它 Pixel Pusher 的应用，挺有趣的。它是一个协作式像素画编辑器。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: pixel art is kind of sort of retro gaming aesthetic
cues.zh: 像素画有点那种复古游戏的美学风格

cues.en: where you try to make
cues.zh: 就是你要用

cues.en: pictures consisting from just this grid of a fairly small number of pixels,
cues.zh: 由相当少量像素组成的网格来画出图像，

cues.en: and people, like, make really cute animations and stuff like that with this. So we took this off the shelf open source implementation by Javier Wallin, I think is his name,
cues.zh: 人们用它做出非常可爱的动画之类的东西。所以我们用了 Javier Wallin（我记得是这个名字）的开源实现，

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: this was just a single user app running in your web browser, and we made it turned it into a collaborative app by building on top of auto merge. So it looks like this. Pixel pusher is our variant,
cues.zh: 这原本只是一个在浏览器里运行的单用户应用，我们通过在 automerge 之上构建，把它变成了协作式应用。所以它看起来是这样的。Pixel Pusher 是我们的版本，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: what we wanted to experiment with this here is not just like the straightforward collaboration where one user makes a change, it shows up on another user's device,
cues.zh: 我们想在这里试验的，不只是那种简单的协作——一个用户做出更改，就显示在另一个用户的设备上，

cues.en: but also wanted to think about, like, for example, with git, you get pull requests,
cues.zh: 还想考虑比如像 git 里的 pull request 那样的机制，

cues.en: which is a mechanism by which a user can suggest some changes and then the maintainer of a repository can accept or not accept, or maybe accept with some changes.
cues.zh: 也就是用户可以提出一些更改，然后仓库维护者可以接受或不接受，或者带着一些修改再接受。

cues.en: Or with Google Docs, there's this feature for suggesting changes and making comments.
cues.zh: 或者用 Google Docs，它有个功能可以建议修改和发表评论。

cues.en: And so we wanted to explore a bit like what would a similar kind of suggesting changes like user interface look like for a collaborative pixel art editor. So then the top right hand side, there's this bit of user interface where you can actually see there are several different versions of the document. So the base document contains just the eyeballs,
cues.zh: 所以我们想探索一下，对于协作式像素画编辑器来说，类似的建议修改式用户界面会是什么样子。在右上角，有一块用户界面，你可以看到文档有好几个不同的版本。基础文档里只有眼球，

cues.en: but then there's one variant that is like a potato man, and so another variant, and you can switch back and forth between those variants.
cues.zh: 但有一个变体是土豆人，还有一个变体，你可以在这些变体之间来回切换。

cues.en: Any user can create their own copy, and then another user, if they like it, can merge that into their local, kind of like a pull request but just with a very lightweight user interface.
cues.zh: 任何用户都可以创建自己的副本，然后另一个用户如果喜欢的话，可以把它合并到本地，有点像 pull request，但界面非常轻量。

cues.zh: 我们就给用户显示个小提示说：“顺便提一下，这里附近有一些改动。你可能需要检查合并后的结果是不是通顺的英文句子，这我们判断不了。”不过，

cues.en: I think that's about as much conflict resolution as you might need here.
cues.zh: 我觉得在这里，这大概就是你所需要的全部冲突解决了。

cues.en: So I'd I'd like to show you just briefly before we wrap up here how the algorithm behind this works, because I think it's kind of neat. And so although you don't need to implement this kind of algorithm yourself, it's kind of cool to see what happens here. So let's take as example a document consisting of the letters h, e, l, and o,
cues.zh: 在结束之前，我想简要介绍一下背后的算法原理，因为我觉得它很巧妙。虽然你不需要自己去实现这种算法，但了解内部机制还是挺酷的。我们来看一个例子，一份包含字母 h、e、l、o 的文档，

cues.en: and we have two concurrent edits happening to this document. So one user adds a second l to make it read hello,
cues.zh: 此时有两个并发编辑发生在这份文档上。一位用户补上了第二个 l，使其变成 hello，

cues.en: and the other
cues.zh: 而另一位

cues.en: user, the purple user on the right, adds an exclamation mark at the end.
cues.zh: 用户，也就是右边的紫色用户，在末尾加了个感叹号。

cues.en: So the way the CRDT works
cues.zh: CRDT 的运作方式是，

cues.en: is it gives each character in the document a unique identifier,
cues.zh: 它会为文档中的每个字符分配一个唯一标识符，

cues.en: and it has a particular scheme for creating those identifiers,
cues.zh: 并且有一套特定的机制来生成这些标识符，

cues.en: and that is it consists of a number, which is just like a counter,
cues.zh: 具体来说，它由一个类似于计数器的数字，

cues.en: and the a and b here is the name of the node that created this particular list element. So node a on the left
cues.zh: 以及创建该特定列表元素的节点名称（这里的 a 和 b）组成。左边的节点 a

cues.en: creates
cues.zh: 创建带有 a 的

cues.en: new list elements with a, and node b here creates a new list element for b, so using the node name b.
cues.zh: 新列表元素，而这里的节点 b 则使用节点名称 b 来创建新的列表元素。

cues.en: And so because each node increments the counter for every operation that's generated and two different nodes will have different names, so that makes these identifiers unique
cues.zh: 因为每个节点都会为生成的每个操作递增计数器，而两个不同节点的名称不同，所以这使得这些标识符在所有节点上都是唯一的。

cues.en: across all of the nodes.
cues.zh: 在所有节点上。

cues.en: And so now,
cues.zh: 所以现在，

cues.en: when
cues.zh: 当

cues.en: these nodes exchange data, it might be via a server or any kind of network, it doesn't really matter, What they exchange is these operations which say insert
cues.zh: 这些节点交换数据时，可能通过服务器或任何网络，这并不重要，它们交换的是这些操作，比如说插入

cues.en: a new list element, new character L,
cues.zh: 一个新的列表元素，新字符 L，

cues.en: with ID 4A, so that's the new ID given to this new element,
cues.zh: ID 为 4A，这是给这个新元素的新 ID，

cues.en: after
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: the existing list element with ID 2A. So this is important. It doesn't say, like, insert at position 15
cues.zh: 现有列表元素 ID 2A 之后。这很重要。它并不是说，插入到位置 15

cues.en: because position 15 might change if somebody inserts or deletes something before position 15. So instead, we use these identifiers
cues.zh: 因为如果有人在位置 15 之前插入或删除东西，位置 15 可能会变化。所以我们改用这些标识符

cues.en: as a way of reliably
cues.zh: 作为一种可靠的方式

cues.en: pointing to a particular position in the sequence.
cues.zh: 指向序列中的特定位置。

cues.en: And the other user similarly creates this operation that says insert exclamation mark with ID 4B after the existing element 3A, which is the O.
cues.zh: 另一个用户同样创建了这个操作，说插入感叹号，ID 为 4B，在现有元素 3A 之后，也就是 O 之后。

cues.en: And so these messages simply get forwarded on to the two users,
cues.zh: 所以这些消息只是被转发给两个用户，

cues.en: and they each apply exactly what
cues.zh: 他们各自应用完全

cues.en: you would expect.
cues.zh: 符合预期的操作。

cues.en: So the purple one here looks for the character with ID 3A and puts the exclamation mark with 4B after the 3A, so it doesn't matter that the position has shifted along by one. This unique identifier still clearly identifies the position
cues.zh: 所以这里的紫色用户找到 ID 为 3A 的字符，把 ID 为 4B 的感叹号放在 3A 之后，所以位置偏移了一位也没关系。这个唯一标识符仍然清楚地标识了位置

cues.en: where to insert,
cues.zh: 插入到哪里，

cues.en: and we just need, this doesn't rely on any ordering guarantees particularly,
cues.zh: 我们只需要，这并不特别依赖任何顺序保证，

cues.en: so this can just go through any kind of network.
cues.zh: 所以这可以穿过任何类型的网络。

cues.en: So you might realize that I haven't told you about one of the issues, which is what happens if two people insert in the same place in the same document?
cues.zh: 你可能意识到，我还没提到其中一个问题：如果两个人在同一文档的同一位置插入内容，会发生什么？

cues.en: And so this one requires a little bit more explanation.
cues.zh: 这个问题需要多解释一下。

cues.en: So imagine we have a document
cues.zh: 假设我们有一个文档

cues.en: that reads a, b, c,
cues.zh: 内容是 a、b、c，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: on the left hand side, the user adds x, y between the a and the b. So it reads a x y b c.
cues.zh: 在左侧，用户在 a 和 b 之间添加了 x、y，所以变成 a x y b c。

cues.en: And independently of that, on the purple side,
cues.zh: 与此同时，在紫色一侧，

cues.en: the letters p and q get added similarly between
cues.zh: 字母 p 和 q 也被类似地添加到了

cues.en: a and b.
cues.zh: a 和 b 之间。

cues.en: And so what we want to ensure is that
cues.zh: 我们要确保的是，

cues.en: still here in this case, everybody ends up in the same state at the end.
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，最终所有人都达到相同的状态。

cues.en: Okay, and so for this,
cues.zh: 好，为此，

cues.en: I'm now going to start with sending that
cues.zh: 我现在先把右侧的

cues.en: insertion of p over from the right hand side to the left hand side. This works as you would expect, so insert P
cues.zh: p 插入操作发送到左侧。这按预期工作，插入 P

cues.en: with ID 4B after 1A.
cues.zh: ID 为 4B，位于 1A 之后。

cues.en: 1A is still there, it's the letter A, so it puts the P directly after A but before the X,
cues.zh: 1A 还在那里，就是字母 A，所以把 P 直接放在 A 之后、X 之前，

cues.en: and then similarly the Q comes across, insert q with ID 5b after 4b.
cues.zh: 然后类似地，Q 也过来了，插入 q，ID 为 5b，位于 4b 之后。

cues.en: So 4b is there, but that's the letter p that we just inserted, so it puts the q after the p. Okay, so that's one direction sorted.
cues.zh: 4b 在那里，但那是我们刚插入的字母 p，所以把 q 放在 p 之后。好，一个方向解决了。

cues.en: We've got a, p, q, x, y, b, c.
cues.zh: 我们得到了 a、p、q、x、y、b、c。

cues.en: Now we need to ensure that if the message is going the opposite direction, we end up in the same state.
cues.zh: 现在需要确保消息往相反方向传时，也能得到相同的状态。

cues.en: And if we just do this naively, so just applying, say, insert 4a after 1a,
cues.zh: 如果天真地直接做，比如应用插入 4a 到 1a 之后，

cues.en: it's actually going to end up with this in the opposite order on the right hand side. So here we need to be a little bit more clever.
cues.zh: 右侧实际上会以相反的顺序结束。所以这里需要更聪明一点。

cues.en: So we need to ensure that the x ends up after the q.
cues.zh: 所以，我们需要确保 X 最终排在 Q 后面。

cues.en: So even though the
cues.zh: 所以，尽管

cues.en: operation for inserting x says insert after 1a,
cues.zh: 插入 X 的操作指示要把它插入到 1A 后面，

cues.en: what we need to do is actually shift along and put it not directly after 1A but after 5B, which is a Q.
cues.zh: 但我们实际需要做的是沿着列表继续移动，不要直接把它插在 1A 后面，而是要放在 5B 后面，因为 5B 是一个 Q。

cues.en: And so for that, we're going to use the following rule.
cues.zh: 为此，我们将使用以下规则。

cues.en: When a new insertion comes in, so in this case, the insertion of 4A comes in after 1A,
cues.zh: 当有新的插入操作到来时，比如这里，要在 1A 后面插入 4A，

cues.en: first of all, we set to our starting position, which is 1A, so we want to insert after 1A.
cues.zh: 首先，我们将当前位置设为起始位置，也就是 1A，因为我们要在 1A 后面插入元素。

cues.en: And now we're going to compare the ID of the new incoming operation
cues.zh: 接下来，我们要比较新到达操作的 ID

cues.en: to the ID of the next element in the list.
cues.zh: 和列表中下一个元素的 ID。

cues.en: And in this case, the next element is 4B,
cues.zh: 在这个例子中，下一个元素是 4B，

cues.en: so it's the P.
cues.zh: 也就是 P。

cues.en: And so what we're going to do now is if the ID of the incoming operation is less
cues.zh: 接下来，如果新到达操作的 ID 小于

cues.en: than the ID of the next element in the list, we're going to skip over that element
cues.zh: 列表中下一个元素的 ID，我们就跳过这个元素，

cues.en: and move on, so move one further to the right, and we'll repeat the same thing. So now we look at the next next element in the list, which is q.
cues.zh: 继续向右移动一位，然后重复相同的操作。现在，我们查看列表中再下一个元素，也就是 Q。

cues.en: Q has an ID of 5b.
cues.zh: Q 的 ID 是 5B。

cues.en: 5b is also greater than 4a,
cues.zh: 5B 也大于 4A，

cues.en: so we're going to skip over it as well. So apply the same rule. Skip over
cues.zh: 所以我们同样跳过它。继续应用这条规则：跳过

cues.en: any of the elements that have a greater ID than the one we're inserting.
cues.zh: 所有 ID 大于当前待插入元素 ID 的元素。

cues.en: And so then we've skipped over Q.
cues.zh: 这样，我们就跳过了 Q。

cues.en: Now the next
cues.zh: 接下来

cues.en: element to look at is the letter B, which has an ID of 2A. 2A is less than 4A,
cues.zh: 要查看的元素是字母 B，它的 ID 是 2A。2A 小于 4A，

cues.en: so now we stop the skipping, and this is where we insert
cues.zh: 所以这时我们停止跳过，并在这里插入

cues.en: the letter X.
cues.zh: 字母 X。

cues.en: And so this rule,
cues.zh: 所以这条规则，

cues.en: it does actually work. It takes a little bit of convincing,
cues.zh: 确实有效。这需要一点说服力，

cues.en: and this is why we did all of that formal proof stuff, because it's not entirely obvious immediately
cues.zh: 这就是为什么我们做了所有那些形式化证明的工作，因为它并不是一眼就能看出来的

cues.en: that this actually does the right thing. But it turns out that it does actually always do the right thing. Now finally, for the insertion of y, this one is easy again, because here now we have just insert y with id 5a after id 4a. 4a is that x that we've already placed in the list, so now we can just put it directly after the x.
cues.zh: 这确实能正确工作。但事实证明它确实总是能正确工作。最后，对于 y 的插入，这个又很简单了，因为现在这里我们只需要把 y 插到 id 4a 之后，id 为 5a。4a 就是我们已经放进列表的那个 x，所以现在我们可以直接把它放在 x 后面。

cues.en: Just to show you that the skipping doesn't happen in any other circumstances, so this 5a is not going to skip over 2a because 2a is less than 5a. On the other side here, this insertion of p, 4b,
cues.zh: 只是为了向你展示，跳过不会在其他情况下发生，所以这个 5a 不会跳过 2a，因为 2a 小于 5a。在另一边这里，这个 p 的插入，4b，

cues.en: will not skip over the x here because for b is greater than for a, so for b will not skip over for a.
cues.zh: 不会跳过这里的 x，因为 4b 大于 4a，所以 4b 不会跳过 4a。
